title: Grit
author: Angela Duckworth
blurb: Psychologist Angela Duckworth asks why some people achieve so much more than others with similar ability. Her answer is grit, a blend of passion and perseverance for a long-term goal. Drawing on her research with West Point cadets, spelling bee finalists, salespeople and students, she shows that grit often predicts success better than talent or test scores. She argues that talent matters, but effort counts twice: once in building skill and again in turning skill into achievement. Gritty people tend to share four traits. They have a deep interest, they practice deliberately, they feel a sense of purpose, and they hold on to hope after setbacks. Duckworth's encouraging message is that grit is not fixed. It can be grown from the inside, and also from the outside through supportive parents, challenging activities and cultures that value persistence.
